free_tier.stated: none for a new user: the register page says no new sign-ups are accepted for the API and points to a free IP2Location.io API; a key issued earlier was limited to 2 queries a second
free_tier.notes: the page says a faster key from IP2Location.io offers 30K IP geolocation queries a month; that offer has its own record.

per_object_cap.stated: one IP address per request (the ip parameter, default the caller)

retention.stated: not stated; the page suggests keeping the geolocation in a cookie instead of querying on every page view

egress.terms: not applicable: raw, XML or JSON answers, not metered in bytes

interface_detail: GET https://api.ipinfodb.com/v3/ip-country/ and /v3/ip-city/ with the key, ip and format parameters (raw, xml or json)
tooling: any HTTP client; PHP, Ruby, Python, C#, VB.NET and Java examples are on the page
chaining: No new key can be created; the register page names the IP2Location.io free API as the replacement. Bulk path: none.

limits.value: 2 queries per second; a faster IP is temporarily blocked and then permanently banned

binding_note: no new key can be created, so no limit can be reached by a new user.

identity_cost.detail: the former sign-up gave a free key; the register page now says no new sign-ups are accepted

reliability_note: past 2 queries a second an IP address is temporarily blocked by a firewall and then permanently banned; the origin answers HTTP 403 to a plain client and the pages were read from stored copies
confidence_note: The API page and the register page were quoted on 2026-11-02 from stored copies, because the origin answers HTTP 403 to direct reads; whether keys issued earlier still answer was not tested.

evidence.proved: new sign-ups for the API are closed
evidence.quote: We are no longer accepting new sign ups for the IPInfoDB API.

evidence.proved: the page points to a free IP2Location.io API
evidence.quote: Instead, please sign up for a free IP2Location.io IP Geolocation API, which offers a faster API with more geolocation data points.

evidence.proved: the API page answers HTTP 403 to a plain client
the 403 is a Cloudflare managed challenge
the free service is limited to 2 queries a second
evidence.quote: To remain the stabilities of free service, a rate limit of 2 queries per second applied to our API servers.

evidence.proved: a faster IP is temporarily blocked
evidence.quote: Any IP querying the API faster than this rate will be temporarily blocked by our firewall.

evidence.proved: a request takes one IP address, defaulting to the caller
evidence.quote: | ip | No | Client IP | IPv4 or IPv6 address. |

evidence.proved: a key from a free account is required
evidence.quote: | key | Yes | API key provided with your free account. |

evidence.proved: the page suggests storing the geolocation in a cookie
evidence.quote: - If you track your visitors, avoid querying our API for all your page views (you can store the geolocation in a cookie, see below for an example).

notes: Free requests: none for new users; sign-ups are closed. Rate limit: 2 queries a second, blocked then banned past it. Bulk path: none. The replacement named on the register page is IP2Location.io, which has its own record.
